topic: Nuisance-uniform minimax outcome annotation for an overlapping finite causal-policy menu. In a finite-stratum binary-treatment model with known propensities, a frozen rank-full menu of at least three overlapping policies, budgeted outcome-acquisition rates bounded away from zero, and unrestricted eta-positive probabilities on a fixed finite outcome support, derive the local Gaussian policy-contrast experiment uniformly over the full Qh+Nu treatment-effect fiber and every outcome-shape nuisance tangent. Characterize the minimax welfare-regret value V* over deterministic limiting annotation designs; give certified finite-grid upper and lower computation; and construct a vanishing-pilot, stabilized design selector, joint AIPW contrast estimator, and Gaussian minimax rule attaining V*. For the stated rational three-policy witness with H=[-1,1]^2, prove that the unique minimizer of maximum pairwise contrast variance has regret above 0.1965 while a feasible design has regret below 0.18453, and extend the strict separation to an explicit open parameter neighborhood. Consumer: prospective independent validation of the eight azithromycin rules in the ABCD trial, where targeted follow-up replaces uniform or exogenous outcome collection. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A saturated mean/shape decomposition gives orthogonal Fisher information and T_r' I_r T_r=Sigma(r)^(-1); bounded likelihood-ratio arguments support the full-nuisance lower-risk transfer. A projected nested-cell selector handles nonunique optima, and exact conditional AIPW covariance plus rectangle-risk transfer support attainment. Outward-rounded Arb certificates verify L(r_alt)<0.18453, L(r_G)>0.1965 and separation on a radius-10^-6 neighborhood. Tests covered shape nuisances, pilot information, discontinuous selectors, boundary minima, zero-regret sets, variance degeneracy, and current policy-design collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete a measurable implementation theorem coupling the certified nested-cell design sieve and Gaussian observation-grid selector, with locally uniform risk attainment and deterministic optimal-rate convergence at every nonunique optimum. EARLY KILL TEST: Verify nested-cell stabilization at separated tied minima and a dyadic-boundary minimum under uniform approximation errors; failure to stabilize every fixed tree prefix stops universal attainment. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_policy_disagreement_annotation.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior design arguments control a finite plug-in selector through positive separation from nonoptimal designs; uniform criterion convergence on a compact continuum yields only convergence to the argmin set and does not stabilize a canonical representative when minima are tied or lie on dyadic cell boundaries. The literature likewise treats pilot convergence to a unique allocation, adaptive AIPW under already-stabilized probabilities, and nonunique policy optima separately. The first missing step is a nested-cell measurable-selection lemma whose every fixed tree prefix stabilizes under uniform approximation error, followed by a joint coupling that remains valid despite discontinuities of both the selected design and the Gaussian policy rule.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable nested-cell selection theorem with an explicit pilot schedule and deterministic distance-to-canonical-optimum modulus, together with a joint pilot/main-sample coupling proving locally uniform convergence of implemented welfare regret to the deterministic-design minimax value at every separated tie and boundary optimum.

writing_exemplar.why: Its costly-ground-truth annotation problem and pilot-to-main-batch workflow provide the closest motivation arc for a universal implementation result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ground-truth outcomes are costly -> the best annotation design depends on unknown outcome variation -> a pilot must learn that design -> tied regret optima require a measurable stabilized selector with uniform risk guarantees

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate design-indexed efficient-influence-function criteria from a pilot, enforce the acquisition budget, and couple the learned design to a one-step main-sample estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest pilot-to-efficient-design proof, but the destination replaces a regular componentwise objective with nonsmooth Gaussian regret and a nonunique compact argmin.

method_exemplars.technique: Use predictable stabilized probabilities and martingale central-limit arguments to establish an efficient AIPW limit law under adaptive data collection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The joint policy-contrast estimator needs the same predictable-weight controls after the annotation design has been selected measurably.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace naive smooth-argmax reasoning at nonunique optima with inference explicitly adapted to exceptional laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its exceptional-law analysis isolates the same failure of ordinary continuous-mapping arguments that tied annotation optima create.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior Gaussian-game construction reduces binary choice to signed endpoint states and explicitly excludes multiple actions and design-indexed covariance, while the adjacent annotation proposal supplies only a scalar ATE experiment. Web literature either optimizes one influence-function variance, compares coordinatewise efficiency, or treats mutually exclusive actions. Overlapping policies instead create a nonexchangeable joint AIPW contrast covariance, simplex-valued rules, and higher-order tie faces; welfare regret is not a monotone function of the largest marginal contrast variance. The signed-endpoint reduction must therefore be replaced by a finite action-regret experiment before annotation rates are optimized.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact saddle representation of the K-policy Gaussian welfare-regret value indexed by feasible annotation rates, existence and characterization of a minimax simplex-valued rule and least-favorable distribution, and an explicit regime-level counterexample in which the maximum-pairwise-variance design is strictly regret-suboptimal.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction moves directly from a constrained data-collection budget to downstream welfare and explains why familiar allocation surrogates need not optimize regret.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Follow-up resources are limited -> collection should serve the eventual treatment decision -> minimax regret changes the optimal allocation -> overlapping policies require covariance-aware outcome annotation

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce many-action treatment choice to a Gaussian zero-sum decision problem and analyze its minimax rule through finite-game methods.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is also a finite-action Gaussian game, but its nonexchangeable covariance is controlled by a shared outcome-annotation design.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive annotation probabilities from an efficient-influence-function variance objective, learn them in a pilot batch, and use doubly robust AIPW estimation with missing outcomes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the annotation and AIPW machinery that must be lifted from one scalar influence function to the full policy-contrast vector.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert budgeted multidimensional two-phase design into finite-dimensional optimization using efficient influence functions and a pilot-based one-step estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its multidimensional design reduction is structurally closest, although componentwise maximin efficiency must be replaced by joint policy-menu regret.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The local-decision, local-direction-uniformity, and double-sampling arguments occur in separate literatures and do not compose automatically. Mean-preserving outcome-shape scores alter likelihood ratios while leaving policy contrasts fixed, and the annotation design determines which score components are observed. The missing proof step is a uniform quadratic likelihood expansion followed by nuisance projection with remainders controlled over the full fiber; a pointwise LAN statement is insufficient because the lower-risk transfer must remain valid across all shape tangents and feasible designs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nuisance-uniform LAN or Le Cam convergence theorem identifying the policy-contrast central sequence and design-indexed covariance, plus a locally uniform asymptotic minimax inequality and matching Gaussian-risk transfer over the specified treatment-effect and outcome-shape tangent sets.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames treatment choice as a decision problem rather than ordinary point estimation and uses the Gaussian limit experiment as the bridge to asymptotic optimality.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment choice is not ordinary estimation -> local alternatives determine first-order welfare regret -> localization yields a Gaussian decision experiment -> outcome annotation requires that reduction uniformly over unobserved shape nuisances

method_exemplars.technique: Use LAN and convergence of experiments to reduce treatment choice to a Gaussian minimax problem and transfer its lower bound to the original experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is a vector-valued, design-indexed, nuisance-uniform strengthening of this Gaussian reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Transform full-data influence functions under double sampling, derive the observed-data efficient influence function, and construct robust sample-split estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Planned annotation is an observed-data projection problem of the same form, and the projected influence vector determines the required contrast covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Control policy regret uniformly over local fluctuation directions using empirical-process convergence to a Gaussian limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its perturbation-uniform argument is analogous to the needed fiber uniformity, with design-dependent missingness supplying the new obstacle.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing exact calculations are predominantly binary or symmetry-driven, while many-action work supplies computational games without a validated-numerics theorem for the nested optimization over designs, Gaussian rules, and local effect vectors. Here covariance is non-diagonal and design-dependent, worst cases may lie on policy-tie cones or truncation boundaries, and minimizers may be nonunique. Floating-point grids can therefore miss maximizers or reverse a strict design comparison. The missing first step is a uniform approximation modulus simultaneously controlling effect-parameter discretization, Gaussian observation truncation, rule discretization, and optimization error.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-grid certification theorem giving computable upper and lower bounds on the continuous Gaussian minimax value with explicit mesh and tail errors, together with outward-rounded interval certificates for strict regret separation and a continuity modulus extending it to a stated open parameter neighborhood.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents many-action minimax regret as both a decision-theoretic and computational problem, providing the closest framing for why certification matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many actions make exact minimax rules difficult -> Gaussian limits and computational games make approximation possible -> policy overlap makes covariance design-dependent -> rigorous finite-grid bounds are needed to certify design comparisons

method_exemplars.technique: Represent finite treatment choice as a zero-sum computational game and exploit Gaussian limit structure to evaluate minimax regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate starts from the same game reduction and adds explicit mesh, tail, and interval-enclosure bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Match change-of-measure regret lower bounds with central-limit and large-deviation upper bounds under a variance-learned allocation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It analytically closes the design-level regret claim in the binary case; certified grids replace the unavailable closed form for overlapping multi-policy choice.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a stacked covariance matrix for several doubly robust rule-value estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: That joint covariance is the empirical input whose induced Gaussian decision risk the certified solver must bound.

open_problems.open_problem: How should prospective targeted follow-up in an independent ABCD-like azithromycin validation cohort be allocated to jointly compare the eight frozen clinical policies and minimize worst-case welfare loss from selecting the wrong policy?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The ABCD studies provide a concrete finite policy menu and already recognize dependence among doubly robust rule-value estimates, but they evaluate outcomes already collected and do not choose which future outcomes to acquire. Because the policies overlap, following one child informs several contrasts simultaneously, and the most valuable stratum-treatment cell depends on the entire covariance and on which near-tied policies can cause welfare loss. Scalar ATE annotation formulas and separate confidence intervals therefore do not solve the downstream selection problem. The first changed proof step is derivation of the exact conditional joint AIPW covariance under prospective annotation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A pre-specifiable two-phase validation design and joint AIPW contrast estimator with a multivariate limit law, paired with a finite-menu Gaussian minimax rule whose locally uniform welfare regret attains the optimal deterministic annotation-design value for the eight frozen policies.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination-area motivation: targeted antibiotics must balance benefit, diagnostic feasibility, and antimicrobial resistance while current rules disagree.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Broad azithromycin use risks resistance -> personalized rules target children likely to benefit -> competing rules disagree and some comparisons are imprecise -> prospective follow-up should be designed to select among the frozen rules

method_exemplars.technique: Stack rule-specific doubly robust influence-function vectors, estimate their joint covariance, and use cross-fitting for simultaneous rule comparisons.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It constructs the multivariate policy-value object needed by the destination; the missing layer is prospective annotation optimized for selection risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate outcome variation in a pilot batch, allocate costly labels through an estimated optimal probability, and analyze the final AIPW estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest outcome-follow-up design, but must be generalized from scalar ATE variance to correlated eight-rule contrasts and welfare regret.

method_exemplars.technique: Build policy learning from doubly robust scores and connect semiparametric score quality to utilitarian policy regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the bridge from efficient causal scores to welfare performance that the validation design would specialize to a fixed finite menu.

literature_map:
Manski (2004, Econometrica) established minimax-regret treatment rules as a welfare criterion distinct from testing.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica) supplied the local Gaussian and semiparametric minimax bridge for treatment choice.
Stoye (2009, Journal of Econometrics) showed that exact finite-sample minimax computation is difficult even for two treatments.
Masten (2023, Japanese Economic Review) extended Gaussian minimax treatment choice to many treatments using computational-game ideas.
Hu, Zhu, Brunskill, and Wager (2024, arXiv:2403.01386) showed that regret-optimal sample selection can differ from proportional or variance-oriented designs.
Kato (2025, arXiv:2512.08513) proved two-stage Neyman allocation minimax for binary treatment choice, leaving correlated multi-policy annotation outside its scope.
Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018, Econometrica) and Athey and Wager (2021, Econometrica) anchor welfare and doubly robust policy learning while taking observation design as given.
Luedtke and Chambaz (2020, AIHP) obtained regret bounds uniform over local directions; Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Annals of Statistics) exposed nonregularity at nonunique optima.
Gilbert, Yu, and Rotnitzky (2014) and McIsaac and Cook (2015) developed optimal and pilot-adaptive two-phase designs for scalar targets.
Levis et al. (2024, Statistics in Medicine) developed efficient robust causal estimators under double sampling of informatively missing outcomes.
Wang, Wang, and Miao (2026, Statistica Sinica; arXiv:2312.10596) entered multidimensional two-phase design using componentwise efficiency rather than joint policy regret.
Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026, AISTATS; arXiv:2502.10605) directly optimized costly causal outcome annotation, but only for scalar ATE variance.
Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, CLeaR) supplied adaptive AIPW limit theory under stabilized probabilities, not set-valued design selection.
Codi et al. (2025, medRxiv) compared eight ABCD azithromycin rules using a joint doubly robust covariance; Kim et al. (2025, Nature Communications) documented rule disagreement, imprecision, and external-validity limits.
The unoccupied intersection is nuisance-uniform, regret-optimal outcome annotation for a correlated frozen policy menu, with measurable pilot stabilization and rigorous numerical certification.

The closest pilot-design source was downgraded qid stat_longterm_measurement_design/v1; angle0 reviewer strengthening paths emphasize tie conventions, mis-selection control, and pilot-estimable certificates.

Accepted qid stat_discrete_optimal_value_minimax_matched/jackson_factorial yielded a sharp overlap-cone constant question, likewise dropped for topic relevance.
